title: Regret matching, fictitious play, and self-play Nim
brief: Drive rock-paper-scissors and a 2x2 game to their Nash equilibria with regret matching and fictitious play, measure exploitability, and let one Q table learn Nim by playing itself.
hints: exploitability is np.max(A @ y) - np.min(x @ A): the row player's best payoff against y, minus the payoff the column player could hold the row player to against x.
In regret_matching, the column player's payoff vector is u_y = -(x @ A), because it loses what the row player wins. Using +(x @ A) sends it toward the worst strategy.
Add each round's strategies to running sums before you update the regrets, and divide the sums by iters at the end. The average, not the last strategy, is what converges.
Round 0 of regret_matching plays x0 and y0. From round 1 on, play regret_matching_strategy(regret_x) and regret_matching_strategy(regret_y).
In nim_self_play, the target after taking k from n is 1.0 when n - k == 0, else -Q[n - k, legal[n - k]].max(). The minus sign is the whole trick of self-play in a zero-sum game.
